conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-01-01.question: In Genesis 1:4, God saw that the light was good.
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-01-01.learningObjective: Observe that God sees and approves what he makes.
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-01-01.feedbackCorrect: The text says it: God looked at the light he made and saw that it was good.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread the start of Genesis 1:4: God saw that the light was good.

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-01-01.hint: Look at the start of the verse.

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-01-02.question: In Genesis 1:1, tap who created the heavens and the earth.
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-01-02.learningObjective: Identify God as the author of creation.
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-01-02.feedbackCorrect: God is the subject of the Bible's first sentence: he is the one who creates.

feedbackWrong.b: "No princípio" (in the beginning) tells when, not who.
feedbackWrong.c: The earth is what was created, not who created.

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-01-02.hint: Look for who does the action of creating.

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-01-03.question: According to Genesis 1:5, what name did God give the darkness?
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-01-03.learningObjective: Observe that God names the light and the darkness.
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-01-03.feedbackCorrect: God calls the light Day and the darkness Night: he names even the dark.

feedbackWrong.b: The deep appears in Genesis 1:2; here God names the darkness.
feedbackWrong.c: Day is the name God gave the light, not the darkness.
feedbackWrong.d: Evening and morning mark the first day; the darkness has another name.

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-01-03.hint: Read the first sentence of the verse, up to the period.

options.a: Night
options.b: Deep
options.c: Day

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-01-04.question: Put Genesis 1:2 in the order of the text.
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-01-04.feedbackCorrect: That is the verse's order: empty earth, darkness, and the Spirit present over the waters.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the formless earth; the Spirit of God appears at the end of the verse.

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-01-04.hint: The verse starts with the earth.

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-01-05.question: In Genesis 1:3, what does God do so that there is light?
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-01-05.learningObjective: Remember that God creates by his word.
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-01-05.feedbackCorrect: God speaks, and the light comes to be: his word creates.

feedbackWrong.b: God does not ask anyone: he himself speaks, and it happens.
feedbackWrong.c: The text shows God speaking out loud, not just thinking.

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-01-05.hint: Look at the first word of the verse.

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-01-06.question: What does Genesis 1:1 communicate that connects to this context?
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-01-06.learningObjective: Connect Genesis 1:1 to the idea that God comes before everything.
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-01-06.feedbackCorrect: "No princípio, Deus": when everything begins, he is already there, creating.

feedbackWrong.b: The text gives the beginning an author: God created.
feedbackWrong.c: The world has a beginning; God is already there when it begins.

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-01-06.hint: See who is already present in the first sentence.

options.a: God was already there at the beginning
options.b: The beginning had no author
options.c: God came into being along with the world

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-01-01.question: In Genesis 1:1–2, the earth God created was still formless, and the text marks this contrast.
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-01-01.learningObjective: Understand the contrast between Genesis 1:1 and 1:2.
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-01-01.feedbackCorrect: "Porém" turns the page: God created everything, but the earth still awaited form.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread the start of Genesis 1:2: the earth, however, was formless and empty.

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-01-01.hint: Notice the word that links the two verses.

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-01-02.question: In Genesis 1:3, tap the word that shows the result of God's command.
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-01-02.learningObjective: Recognize that God's word brings about what it says.
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-01-02.feedbackCorrect: "E houve luz": what God says happens at once, without delay.

feedbackWrong.a: "Haja" (let there be) is the command itself; the result comes after the semicolon.
feedbackWrong.c: "Disse" (said) opens the scene with God speaking; the result comes at the end.

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-01-03.question: How does Genesis 1:3 relate to the empty earth of Genesis 1:2?
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-01-03.learningObjective: Relate the emptiness of 1:2 to the creating word of 1:3.
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-01-03.feedbackCorrect: The earth was empty and dark; God speaks, and the light begins to change the scene.

feedbackWrong.a: The light comes after "Disse Deus": his word makes it exist.
feedbackWrong.b: The darkness remains until God speaks; he separates light from darkness later.
feedbackWrong.c: The scene stays on the same earth; God acts upon it.

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-01-03.hint: See what happens right after the description of the empty earth.

options.a: The light appears on its own, without God acting
options.b: The darkness vanishes before God speaks
options.c: God creates another world, far from the empty earth
options.d: God's word begins to give form to the emptiness

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-01-04.question: How does the scene move forward in Genesis 1:4–5?
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-01-04.feedbackCorrect: God looks and approves, then separates, and finally gives each part a name.

feedbackWrong.default: First God sees that the light is good; the names come last, in Genesis 1:5.

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-01-04.hint: The names arrive in the second verse.

options.a: God approves the light he made
options.b: God separates the light from the darkness
options.c: God names the day and the night

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-01-05.question: In Genesis 1:2, what was the Spirit of God doing over the waters?
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-01-05.learningObjective: Understand God's presence before the order.
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-01-05.feedbackCorrect: The Spirit hovered: God is present over the empty earth before his first word.

feedbackWrong.b: The text does not speak of breath here; it shows the Spirit hovering, present.
feedbackWrong.c: The text does not say he walked; it uses the image of someone hovering over the waters.

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-01-05.hint: It is an image of someone staying over something, attentive.

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-01-06.question: What links Genesis 1:3 to Psalm 33:6?
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-01-06.learningObjective: Relate creation by the word in Genesis and in the Psalms.
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-01-06.feedbackCorrect: In both texts God's word is enough: he speaks, and things exist.

feedbackWrong.b: There is no effort: by the word of the Lord the heavens were made.
feedbackWrong.c: Neither text shows a struggle; they show God speaking.

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-01-06.hint: Compare how each text says things came to exist.

options.a: God creates by his word
options.b: God creates little by little, with effort
options.c: The world is born from a struggle

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-01-01.question: Genesis 1:1–2 shows that chaos already existed before God, and he only arranged what he found.
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-01-01.learningObjective: Recognize that the text places nothing before God.
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-01-01.feedbackCorrect: Nothing appears before God: in the beginning, he creates the heavens and the earth.

feedbackWrong.true: The text places nothing before God; the still formless earth is already his work (Gen 1:1).

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-01-01.hint: See who appears first in the text.

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-01-02.question: In Genesis 1:2, tap the phrase that shows God is not far from the still empty earth.
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-01-02.learningObjective: Support from the text that God is present from the start.
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-01-02.feedbackCorrect: The Spirit of God is already there, over the waters, before there is light.

feedbackWrong.a: The deep is the setting, not God's presence.
feedbackWrong.b: The darkness describes the setting; God's presence comes at the end of the verse.

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-01-02.hint: Look for someone, not a place.

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-01-03.question: What reading does Genesis 1:1–2 support about God and the beginning of the world?
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-01-03.learningObjective: Choose the interpretation the text supports about God and the origin of the world.
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-01-03.feedbackCorrect: God is at the beginning of everything, and his Spirit already hovers over the empty earth.

feedbackWrong.a: The Spirit present over the waters rules out a distant God.
feedbackWrong.b: Nothing appears before God: "No princípio, Deus criou".
feedbackWrong.c: The text does not argue: it begins with God already acting.

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-01-03.hint: Compare each option with the start and the end of the passage.

options.a: God created the world and then left it alone
options.b: Before God there was already a chaos with no owner
options.c: The text begins by proving, with arguments, that God exists
options.d: God comes before everything and is present from the start

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-01-04.question: Which sequence shows the thread of creation that begins in Genesis 1:1?
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-01-04.learningObjective: See Genesis 1:1 as the start of a thread that runs through the Bible.
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-01-04.feedbackCorrect: The God who creates in the beginning comes to us in Jesus and, at the end, makes all new.

feedbackWrong.default: Follow the story: creation (Gen 1:1), the Word among us (John 1:14), all new (Rev 21:5).

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-01-04.hint: Follow the order of the Bible's story: beginning, Jesus, end.

options.a: In the beginning, God creates the heavens and the earth
options.b: The Word, through whom all things were made, comes to live among us
options.c: From the throne, God makes all things new

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-01-05.question: In Genesis 1:1, which verb says what God does in the beginning?
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-01-05.learningObjective: Remember the term that carries the meaning of the scene.
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-01-05.feedbackCorrect: God makes exist what did not exist; he does not just arrange something already there.

feedbackWrong.b: God does not find the world ready-made; he makes it exist.
feedbackWrong.c: Organizing assumes something before God; the text says he made the heavens and the earth.

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-01-05.hint: It is the verb that comes right after God.

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-01-06.question: What links Genesis 1:1 to Psalm 90:2?
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-01-06.learningObjective: Connect the start of Genesis to the eternal God of the Psalms.
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-01-06.feedbackCorrect: Before the mountains and the earth, God is already God: he is before all he created.

feedbackWrong.a: The psalm says nothing about the order of mountains and earth; it speaks of God before both.
feedbackWrong.c: Both texts give the world a beginning; only God is from everlasting to everlasting.

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-01-06.hint: See what the psalm says existed before the mountains.

options.a: The mountains came before the earth
options.b: God exists before the world
options.c: The world is eternal like God

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-02-01.question: In Exodus 3:12, God promises Moses that an angel would be with him.
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-02-01.learningObjective: Observe that God promises Moses his own presence.
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-02-01.feedbackCorrect: God sends no one in his place: he himself says "Certamente estarei contigo".

feedbackWrong.true: Reread Exodus 3:12: God himself promises "Certamente estarei contigo" (I will surely be with you).

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-02-01.hint: See who is speaking and whom he is speaking about.

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-02-02.question: In Exodus 3:11, tap the king Moses would have to go to.
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-02-02.learningObjective: Identify before whom Moses would be sent.
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-02-02.feedbackCorrect: Pharaoh was the king of Egypt, the most powerful man Moses would have to face.

feedbackWrong.a: Moses is speaking with God; the king he would have to face is someone else.
feedbackWrong.b: Egypt is the country, not the king.

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-02-02.hint: Look for a king's title right after "ir até" (go to).

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-02-03.question: According to Exodus 3:12, what would be the sign that God sent Moses?
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-02-03.learningObjective: Observe the sign God gives Moses.
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-02-03.feedbackCorrect: The sign would come later: freed from Egypt, the people would serve God on that mountain.

feedbackWrong.b: The text does not promise leaving that same day; the sign comes after the exodus.
feedbackWrong.c: The verse does not speak of Moses' courage; it speaks of the people serving God.
feedbackWrong.d: The bush is not the sign here; the sign is the people on the mountain.

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-02-03.hint: Read what comes after "este será o sinal" (this will be the sign).

options.a: The people, already free, would serve God on that mountain
options.b: Pharaoh would let the people go that same day
options.c: Moses would speak without fear before the king
options.d: The bush would keep burning for years

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-02-04.question: Put Exodus 3:16 in the order of the text.
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-02-04.feedbackCorrect: First the order to gather the elders, then who appeared, and then what God saw.

feedbackWrong.default: The verse begins with the command to Moses; what God saw in Egypt comes at the end.

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-02-04.hint: The verse begins with a command to Moses.

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-02-05.question: In Exodus 3:13, what does Moses imagine the people will ask about God?
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-02-05.learningObjective: Remember the question that leads to the revelation of the name.
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-02-05.feedbackCorrect: The people would want the name of the one who sent Moses, to know who he is.

feedbackWrong.a: Moses does not imagine questions about plans; he imagines questions about who God is.
feedbackWrong.b: The question Moses imagines is not about strength; it is about what God is called.

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-02-05.hint: See the question the people would ask, near the end of the verse.

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-02-06.question: What does Exodus 3:14 communicate that connects to this context?
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-02-06.learningObjective: Connect the revealed name to Moses' mission.
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-02-06.feedbackCorrect: God gives Moses the name he will carry: "EU SOU me enviou a vocês".

feedbackWrong.a: Moses does not go on his own; he goes in the name of the one who sends him.
feedbackWrong.c: Pharaoh does not send Moses; God is the one who sends.

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-02-06.hint: See what Moses must say to the children of Israel.

options.a: Moses goes in his own name
options.b: God names the one who sends him
options.c: Pharaoh authorizes the journey

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-02-01.question: In Exodus 3:11–12, God answers Moses' doubt by praising his qualities.
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-02-01.learningObjective: Understand the contrast between Moses' doubt and God's answer.
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-02-01.feedbackCorrect: God does not talk about Moses' qualities: he answers with his own presence.

feedbackWrong.true: Reread Exodus 3:12: God's answer is "Certamente estarei contigo", not praise.

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-02-01.hint: Compare Moses' question with the first sentence of the answer.

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-02-02.question: In Exodus 3:10, tap the words that mark the purpose of Moses' sending.
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-02-02.learningObjective: Recognize the purpose marker in Moses' call.
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-02-02.feedbackCorrect: "Para que" (so that) opens the purpose: Moses goes to free God's people from Egypt.

feedbackWrong.a: "Vem agora" (come now) is the call; the purpose comes after.
feedbackWrong.b: "Do Egito" (from Egypt) says where the people would leave; the purpose link comes before.

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-02-02.hint: Look for the link in the middle of the verse, after "Faraó".

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-02-03.question: In Exodus 3:14–15, how does the name "EU SOU" (I AM) relate to the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob?
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-02-03.learningObjective: Relate the revealed name to God's history with Israel.
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-02-03.feedbackCorrect: Right after "EU SOU", God presents himself as the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

feedbackWrong.a: God says this is his name forever, from generation to generation.
feedbackWrong.c: The next verse ties the name to Israel's fathers: it is not another God.
feedbackWrong.d: God tells Moses to take the name to the children of Israel; it is no secret.

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-02-03.hint: See how God presents himself right after saying the name.

options.a: It is a title that holds only while the people are in Egypt
options.b: It is the same God who already cared for Israel's fathers
options.c: It is a new God, who replaces the God of their ancestors
options.d: It is a secret name, for Moses alone to know

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-02-04.question: How does the conversation move forward in Exodus 3:11–12?
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-02-04.learningObjective: Understand the movement of the conversation between Moses and God.
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-02-04.feedbackCorrect: Moses looks at himself; God answers with his presence and a sign still to come.

feedbackWrong.default: The conversation begins with Moses' doubt; the sign is the last thing God says.

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-02-04.hint: Who speaks first in this dialogue?

options.a: Moses doubts himself
options.b: God promises his presence
options.c: God gives a sign still to come

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-02-05.question: In Exodus 3:12, what does God promise Moses in answer to his doubt?
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-02-05.learningObjective: Understand that God's presence is the answer to Moses' doubt.
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-02-05.feedbackCorrect: God promises to be with him: his presence answers Moses' "Quem sou eu?".

feedbackWrong.a: The text does not say God would go in his place; it says he would be with him.
feedbackWrong.b: God does not promise to speak for Moses here; he promises to be with him.

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-02-05.hint: It is the first sentence of God's answer.

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-02-06.question: What links Exodus 3:15 to Psalm 9:10?
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-02-06.learningObjective: Relate the revealed name to the trust of God's people.
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-02-06.feedbackCorrect: God gives his name to be known, and those who know him learn to trust him.

feedbackWrong.b: The name holds from generation to generation: the same God for all of them.
feedbackWrong.c: God has the name taken to the people, and the psalm speaks of those who know it.

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-02-06.hint: See what the psalm says about those who know God's name.

options.a: Those who know the name trust
options.b: Each generation has another god
options.c: God's name is a secret

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-02-01.question: In Exodus 3:14, Moses' authority before the people comes from the one who sends him, not from himself.
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-02-01.learningObjective: Interpret Moses' mission as resting on who God is.
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-02-01.feedbackCorrect: Moses shows no credentials of his own: he says that "EU SOU" (I AM) sent him.

feedbackWrong.false: Moses must say "EU SOU me enviou a vocês": the weight is on the one who sends.

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-02-01.hint: See what Moses must say to the people.

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-02-02.question: In Exodus 3:15, tap the word that shows this name of God has no expiry date.
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-02-02.learningObjective: Support from the text that God's name holds forever.
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-02-02.feedbackCorrect: God does not present himself only for that moment: the name is forever.

feedbackWrong.a: "Assim" (thus) introduces what Moses must say, not how long the name holds.
feedbackWrong.b: "Ainda mais" (further) only shows that God keeps speaking.

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-02-02.hint: Look right after "este é o meu nome" (this is my name).

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-02-03.question: What reading does Exodus 3:13–14 support about God's name?
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-02-03.learningObjective: Choose the interpretation the text supports about God's name.
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-02-03.feedbackCorrect: God answers the question and even tells Moses to take the name to the children of Israel.

feedbackWrong.a: Moses speaks of the "Deus de seus pais": "EU SOU" is that same God.
feedbackWrong.b: God answers "EU SOU O QUE SOU" and sends the name to the people: there is no refusal.
feedbackWrong.c: The weight is not on Moses: "EU SOU me enviou a vocês".

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-02-03.hint: See what God tells Moses to do with the name.

options.a: I AM is a new god, different from the God of the fathers
options.b: God refuses to tell Moses his name
options.c: The mission depends on Moses being strong and prepared
options.d: God makes himself known and has his name taken to the people

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-02-04.question: Which sequence shows the promise of Exodus 3:12 being fulfilled?
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-02-04.learningObjective: See in Exodus 3:12 a promise that God keeps.
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-02-04.feedbackCorrect: God promises, frees the people, and brings them to the same mountain: he keeps his word.

feedbackWrong.default: Follow the story: promise (Exod 3:12), leaving Egypt (Exod 12:51), and the mountain (Exod 19:2).

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-02-04.hint: The promise comes first; the mountain is the arrival point.

options.a: God promises the people will serve him on that mountain
options.b: God brings the children of Israel out of Egypt
options.c: Israel camps in front of the mountain of God

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-02-05.question: In Exodus 3:15, how does God say he wants to be kept from generation to generation?
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-02-05.learningObjective: Remember the term that shows God's name passed between generations.
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-02-05.feedbackCorrect: The name is meant to be remembered: each generation knows God by it.

feedbackWrong.b: The text does not speak of fear here; it speaks of memory passed on.
feedbackWrong.c: Worshiping God is good, but the verse speaks of remembering the name.

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-02-05.hint: Look at the end of the verse.

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-02-06.question: What links Exodus 3:14 to John 8:58?
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-02-06.learningObjective: Connect the name revealed at the bush to Jesus' words, as the NT does.
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-02-06.feedbackCorrect: Jesus says "before Abraham was, I AM": he takes the name from the bush for himself.

feedbackWrong.b: Jesus does not say "I was" but "I AM": he speaks of who he is, before Abraham.
feedbackWrong.c: Neither text says that; the point is who says "I AM".

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-02-06.hint: Compare Jesus' last words with the name given to Moses.

options.a: Jesus uses the same "EU SOU" (I AM)
options.b: Jesus speaks only of his age
options.c: Abraham already knew this name

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-03-01.question: In Isaiah 6:2, the seraphim covered their faces with two of their wings.
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-03-01.learningObjective: Observe the seraphim's reaction before the Lord.
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-03-01.feedbackCorrect: The text says it: with two wings each seraph covered its face before the Lord.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread Isaiah 6:2: with two wings each seraph covered its face.

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-03-01.hint: See what each pair of wings was doing.

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-03-02.question: In Isaiah 6:1, tap who Isaiah saw seated on the throne.
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-03-02.learningObjective: Identify whom Isaiah sees in the vision.
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-03-02.feedbackCorrect: Isaiah saw the Lord on the throne, in the very year the king of the land died.

feedbackWrong.b: The temple is the place the robe filled, not who was on the throne.
feedbackWrong.c: King Uzziah had died; the one on the throne in the vision is someone else.

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-03-02.hint: Look for who appears right after "eu vi" (I saw).

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-03-03.question: According to Isaiah 6:4, what happened to the house during the vision?
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-03-03.learningObjective: Observe the effect of the voice in the temple.
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-03-03.feedbackCorrect: The doorposts shake at the voice, and the house fills with smoke.

feedbackWrong.a: There was a voice calling out, so loud that the doorposts moved.
feedbackWrong.b: The text speaks of smoke, not light.
feedbackWrong.c: The doors shake, but the text does not say the house fell.

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-03-03.hint: Read the end of the verse.

options.a: It went completely silent
options.b: It was filled with a bright light
options.c: It collapsed completely

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-03-04.question: Put Isaiah 6:5 in the order of the text.
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-03-04.feedbackCorrect: First the cry, then the confession, and finally what he saw: the King.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with "Ai de mim"; what Isaiah's eyes saw closes the verse.

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-03-04.hint: The verse begins with a cry.

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-03-05.question: In Isaiah 6:2, how many wings did each seraph have?
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-03-05.learningObjective: Remember the description of the seraphim.
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-03-05.feedbackCorrect: Six wings: two covered the face, two the feet, and two were for flying.

feedbackWrong.a: It is fewer than that: the verse describes three pairs of wings.
feedbackWrong.c: Count the pairs in the verse: face, feet, and flight. That is three pairs.

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-03-05.hint: Count the pairs of wings described in the rest of the verse.

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-03-06.question: What does Isaiah 6:1 communicate that connects to this context?
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-03-06.learningObjective: Connect the vision of the throne to Judah's moment of crisis.
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-03-06.feedbackCorrect: The king of the land dies, but Isaiah sees the Lord seated on the throne.

feedbackWrong.a: In the vision the throne is occupied: the Lord is seated on it.
feedbackWrong.b: Isaiah does not take the throne; he sees who is already there.

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-03-06.hint: See who is on the throne in the year the king died.

options.a: The throne was left empty
options.b: Isaiah became the new king
options.c: The Lord still reigns

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-03-01.question: In Isaiah 6:4–5, Isaiah feels lost because the temple was shaking and full of smoke.
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-03-01.learningObjective: Understand the cause of Isaiah's "Ai de mim".
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-03-01.feedbackCorrect: The text gives another reason: Isaiah is unclean, and his eyes have seen the King.

feedbackWrong.true: Reread Isaiah 6:5: the reason is being a man of unclean lips and having seen the King.

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-03-01.hint: See what Isaiah says after "Estou perdido!" (I am lost!).

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-03-02.question: In Isaiah 6:5, tap the word that introduces the reason for the "Ai de mim".
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-03-02.learningObjective: Recognize the cause marker in Isaiah's confession.
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-03-02.feedbackCorrect: "Pois" (for) opens the explanation: he is unclean and has seen the King.

feedbackWrong.a: "Então" (then) marks when Isaiah speaks, not why he speaks.
feedbackWrong.b: "Perdido" (lost) is how he feels; the reason comes right after.

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-03-02.hint: Look at what comes right after Isaiah's cry.

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-03-03.question: How does the seraphim's gesture in Isaiah 6:2 connect to what they proclaim in 6:3?
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-03-03.learningObjective: Relate the seraphim's attitude to the holiness they proclaim.
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-03-03.feedbackCorrect: Those closest to the throne cover their faces and proclaim: God is holy.

feedbackWrong.a: The text does not speak of anger; they praise the Lord's holiness.
feedbackWrong.b: They stand before the Lord; Isaiah is not the center of the scene.
feedbackWrong.d: They fly above the throne; the text does not say they carry it.

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-03-03.hint: Compare what they do with what they say.

options.a: They hide because God is angry with them
options.b: They cover their faces so as not to see Isaiah
options.c: Even they cover their faces before the holy God
options.d: They fly to carry God's throne across the earth

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-03-04.question: How does the scene move forward in Isaiah 6:5–6?
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-03-04.learningObjective: Understand the movement from the confession to the seraph's coming.
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-03-04.feedbackCorrect: Isaiah cries out, confesses his uncleanness, and then a seraph comes to him.

feedbackWrong.default: The coal arrives last, after Isaiah's cry and confession.

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-03-04.hint: The seraph moves only in the second verse.

options.a: Isaiah cries out that he is lost
options.b: Isaiah confesses his and the people's uncleanness
options.c: A seraph comes to him with a coal

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-03-05.question: In Isaiah 6:4, what did the doorposts do at the voice that called out?
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-03-05.learningObjective: Understand the effect of the proclaimed holiness on the temple.
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-03-05.feedbackCorrect: The voice proclaiming holiness makes even the temple's structure shake.

feedbackWrong.a: The text does not speak of doors opening; it speaks of the doorposts shaking.
feedbackWrong.c: Nothing closes in the text; the doorposts shake at the voice.

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-03-05.hint: Think of the effect of a very loud voice on a building.

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-03-06.question: What links Isaiah 6:3 to Revelation 4:8?
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-03-06.learningObjective: Relate Isaiah's vision to the worship in Revelation.
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-03-06.feedbackCorrect: In Isaiah and in Revelation, six-winged beings repeat: "Santo, santo, santo".

feedbackWrong.b: Neither text shows a plea for forgiveness; both show praise.
feedbackWrong.c: The praise does not change: centuries later, the same "Santo, santo, santo" goes on.

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-03-06.hint: Compare what the six-winged beings say in the two texts.

options.a: The same cry before the throne
options.b: The seraphim ask for forgiveness
options.c: The praise changes over time

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-03-01.question: In Isaiah 6:5, Isaiah counts himself among an unclean people instead of thinking he is better than others.
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-03-01.learningObjective: Interpret Isaiah's confession as humility before the holy God.
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-03-01.feedbackCorrect: Before the holy God, Isaiah compares himself to no one: he and the people need God.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread Isaiah 6:5: he says he lives among a people of unclean lips, like himself.

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-03-01.hint: See where Isaiah says he lives.

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-03-02.question: In Isaiah 6:3, tap the phrase that shows God's glory is not confined to the temple.
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-03-02.learningObjective: Support from the text that the holy God's glory fills the world.
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-03-02.feedbackCorrect: The vision happens in the temple, but the holy God's glory fills the whole world.

feedbackWrong.b: "Dos Exércitos" (of hosts) speaks of the Lord's power, not the reach of his glory.
feedbackWrong.c: "Uns aos outros" (to one another) shows how the seraphim proclaim, not how far the glory goes.

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-03-02.hint: Look in the second half of the verse.

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-03-03.question: What reading does Isaiah 6:2–3 support about God's holiness?
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-03-03.learningObjective: Choose the interpretation the text supports about God's holiness.
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-03-03.feedbackCorrect: The seraphim cover their faces and say "santo" three times: God is unlike anything.

feedbackWrong.b: If it were only kindness, the seraphim would not cover their faces before him.
feedbackWrong.c: They cover their faces and proclaim another's holiness: only the Lord is called holy.
feedbackWrong.d: The cry itself says the whole earth is full of his glory.

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-03-03.hint: Compare each option with what the seraphim do and say.

options.a: God is unlike anything, and even the seraphim cover themselves
options.b: Holy just means God is very nice
options.c: The seraphim are almost equal to the Lord
options.d: God is holy only in heaven; the earth is left out

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-03-04.question: Which sequence shows the thread of "Santo, santo, santo" in the Bible?
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-03-04.learningObjective: See Isaiah 6:3 as the start of a thread that runs through the Bible.
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-03-04.feedbackCorrect: Isaiah's vision points to Jesus and goes on in praise that never stops.

feedbackWrong.default: Follow the story: Isaiah (Isa 6:3), the Gospel of John (John 12:41), and Revelation (Rev 4:8).

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-03-04.hint: Start with the prophet and end with the vision at the close of the Bible.

options.a: Isaiah sees the throne and hears the seraphim proclaim holiness
options.b: John says Isaiah saw Jesus' glory
options.c: Before the throne, the holy cry does not stop day or night

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-03-05.question: In Isaiah 6:1, what is the Lord seated on?
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-03-05.learningObjective: Remember the term that shows God's reign in the scene.
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-03-05.feedbackCorrect: The king of the land died, but the Lord still reigns: he is in his place as King.

feedbackWrong.b: The altar appears in Isaiah 6:6; here it is the place from which the Lord reigns.
feedbackWrong.c: The text does not speak of a mountain; it speaks of where the King sits.

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-03-05.hint: Think of the place from which a king rules.

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-03-06.question: What links Isaiah 6:3 to 1 Peter 1:15–16?
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-03-06.learningObjective: Connect God's holiness in Isaiah to the call of his people in the NT.
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-03-06.feedbackCorrect: The God the seraphim call holy calls his people to be holy too.

feedbackWrong.b: Peter asks for holiness "in all your conduct", not only in the temple.
feedbackWrong.c: Peter speaks to those called by God, not to angels.

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-03-06.hint: See why Peter says the people must be holy.

options.a: The Holy One calls us to be holy
options.b: Holiness is only for the temple
options.c: Only angels need to be holy

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-04-01.question: In Psalm 23:2, the Lord leads David beside the still waters.
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-04-01.learningObjective: Observe the shepherd's concrete care in Psalm 23.
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-04-01.feedbackCorrect: The text says it: he leads beside the still waters, as a shepherd does with his sheep.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread the end of Psalm 23:2: he leads me beside the still waters.

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-04-01.hint: Look at the end of the verse.

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-04-02.question: In Psalm 23:1, tap whom David calls his shepherd.
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-04-02.learningObjective: Identify the Lord as the shepherd of the psalm.
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-04-02.feedbackCorrect: David begins with God's name: it is the Lord who cares for him as a shepherd.

feedbackWrong.a: "Nada" (nothing) speaks of what will not be lacking, not of who cares.
feedbackWrong.b: "Meu pastor" (my shepherd) is the title David gives; tap the one who receives it.

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-04-02.hint: Look for who comes before the title at the start of the verse.

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-04-03.question: According to Psalm 23:4, what comforts David in the valley?
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-04-03.learningObjective: Observe what brings David comfort in the valley.
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-04-03.feedbackCorrect: Rod and staff are a shepherd's tools to guide and protect; they comfort David.

feedbackWrong.b: There are no other shepherds in the psalm: "tu estás comigo".
feedbackWrong.c: David does not speak of his own strength; the comfort comes from what is the Lord's.
feedbackWrong.d: The text does not speak of a lamp; it speaks of the rod and the staff.

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-04-03.hint: Read the end of the verse.

options.a: The Lord's rod and staff
options.b: The company of other shepherds
options.c: The strength of his own arm
options.d: The light of a lamp on the way

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-04-04.question: Put Psalm 23:5 in the order of the text.
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-04-04.feedbackCorrect: That is the verse's order: a feast, oil on the head, and an overflowing cup.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the feast; the overflowing cup closes the verse.

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-04-04.hint: The verse begins with the table.

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-04-05.question: In Psalm 23:2, where does the Lord make David lie down?
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-04-05.learningObjective: Remember the concrete image of the shepherd's care.
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-04-05.feedbackCorrect: "Pastos verdejantes" (green pastures): food and rest, chosen by the shepherd.

feedbackWrong.a: The text does not take the sheep up high; it speaks of a green place to rest.
feedbackWrong.b: It seems close, but the text speaks of the place where sheep eat.

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-04-05.hint: Think of the place where sheep eat.

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-04-06.question: What does Psalm 23:1 communicate that connects to this context?
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-04-06.learningObjective: Connect David's experience with sheep to the image of the Lord as shepherd.
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-04-06.feedbackCorrect: The former shepherd now sees himself as a sheep: the Lord does for him what he did for the flock.

feedbackWrong.a: Here the shepherd is the Lord; David places himself as a sheep.
feedbackWrong.c: The psalm does not look to David's past; it speaks of who cares for him now.

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-04-06.hint: See who takes the shepherd's place in the verse.

options.a: David sees himself as the shepherd
options.b: David sees a shepherd in the Lord
options.c: David misses his sheep

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-04-01.question: In Psalm 23:4, David stops being afraid because the Lord takes him out of the valley of the shadow of death.
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-04-01.learningObjective: Understand the reason for David's courage in the valley.
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-04-01.feedbackCorrect: David still walks through the valley; he does not fear because the Lord is with him there.

feedbackWrong.true: Reread: "Ainda que eu ande pelo vale". The reason is another: "porque tu estás comigo".

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-04-01.hint: See what comes after "não temerei mal nenhum" (I will fear no evil).

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-04-02.question: In Psalm 23:4, tap the word that introduces the reason David does not fear.
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-04-02.learningObjective: Recognize the cause marker in the text.
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-04-02.feedbackCorrect: "Porque" (for) opens the reason: the Lord is with him, and that is enough in the valley.

feedbackWrong.a: "Mal nenhum" (no evil) says what David does not fear, not why.
feedbackWrong.b: "Ainda que" (even though) admits the valley's danger; the reason for courage comes later.

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-04-02.hint: Look for the word that links the courage to its reason.

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-04-03.question: How do the two parts of Psalm 23:1 connect?
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-04-03.learningObjective: Relate the shepherd to lacking nothing.
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-04-03.feedbackCorrect: The first sentence supports the second: because the Lord is shepherd, nothing will be lacking.

feedbackWrong.a: It is the other way around: the shepherd comes first, and so nothing is lacking.
feedbackWrong.b: The psalm does not speak of David's achievements, but of the Lord's care.
feedbackWrong.d: David makes no promise; he trusts in what the shepherd will give.

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-04-03.hint: Think about which sentence depends on the other.

options.a: Lacking nothing is the condition for the Lord to be shepherd
options.b: David describes the riches he has already gained
options.c: Having the Lord as shepherd is the reason nothing is lacking
options.d: David promises never to ask the Lord for anything

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-04-04.question: How does the Lord's care move forward in Psalm 23?
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-04-04.feedbackCorrect: From pasture to valley and from valley to table: the Lord cares at every part of the way.

feedbackWrong.default: The psalm starts in the pasture, goes through the valley, and ends at the table and the Lord's house.

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-04-04.hint: The psalm ends in the house of the Lord.

options.a: The shepherd gives rest and direction
options.b: The shepherd goes along in the dark valley
options.c: The Lord serves a feast and welcomes him home

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-04-05.question: In Psalm 23:3, what does the Lord do with David's soul?
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-04-05.learningObjective: Remember the shepherd's action that renews a person.
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-04-05.feedbackCorrect: "Refrigera" means restores strength: the shepherd gives breath back to the weary.

feedbackWrong.b: Keeping appears in other psalms; here the action is renewing the weary soul.
feedbackWrong.c: The psalm does not speak of examining here; it speaks of renewing strength.

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-04-05.hint: It is the action at the start of the verse.

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-04-06.question: What links Psalm 23:1 to Isaiah 40:11?
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-04-06.learningObjective: Relate the image of the Lord as shepherd in Psalms and Isaiah.
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-04-06.feedbackCorrect: In both texts the Lord himself is the shepherd who guides and carries the flock.

feedbackWrong.b: Isaiah shows the opposite: he carries the little lambs in his arms.
feedbackWrong.c: In both texts the shepherd is the Lord, not a human king.

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-04-06.hint: Compare who cares for the flock in the two passages.

options.a: The Lord shepherds his people
options.b: God cares only for the strong
options.c: Kings are the people's shepherds

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-04-01.question: Psalm 23 promises that whoever has the Lord as shepherd does not go through dark valleys.
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-04-01.learningObjective: Distinguish the promise of company from a promise of a life without pain.
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-04-01.feedbackCorrect: The psalm speaks of the valley of death's shadow; the promise is the Lord near, not no valleys.

feedbackWrong.true: Reread Psalm 23:4: "Ainda que eu ande pelo vale". The valley exists; the Lord is in it.

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-04-01.hint: See how the valley verse begins.

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-04-02.question: In Psalm 23:4, tap the phrase that shows the Lord near, not distant.
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-04-02.learningObjective: Support from the text that the holy God cares up close.
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-04-02.feedbackCorrect: "Tu estás comigo": in the darkest place, the Lord is not far; he is at David's side.

feedbackWrong.a: The valley is the place of danger, not the Lord's presence.
feedbackWrong.c: "Não temerei" (I will not fear) is David's reaction; the reason lies in the Lord's presence.

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-04-02.hint: Look for a presence, not a place or a feeling.

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-04-03.question: What reading does Psalm 23:1 support about the Lord?
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-04-03.learningObjective: Choose the reading the text supports about God's care.
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-04-03.feedbackCorrect: "Meu pastor": the Lord is not only everyone's God; he cares for David personally.

feedbackWrong.b: The psalm speaks of the valley of the shadow of death (Ps 23:4); the Lord is in it.
feedbackWrong.c: What is not lacking is the shepherd's care, not every wish David has.
feedbackWrong.d: David calls the Lord "meu pastor": the holy one does not stay far away.

options.a: The Lord cares for David up close, as a shepherd
options.b: With the Lord near, there are no dark valleys
options.c: Whoever has the Lord gets everything they want
options.d: God is too holy to care for anyone up close

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-04-04.question: Which sequence shows the shepherd thread that runs through Psalm 23:1?
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-04-04.learningObjective: See Psalm 23 as the start of a thread that reaches Jesus.
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-04-04.feedbackCorrect: David's shepherd appears in Jesus, who gives his life, and guides his people to the end.

feedbackWrong.default: Follow the story: David's psalm (Ps 23), Jesus (John 10:11), and the end (Rev 7:17).

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-04-04.hint: Follow the Bible's order: Psalms, Gospels, Revelation.

options.a: David calls the Lord his shepherd
options.b: Jesus, the good Shepherd, gives his life for the sheep
options.c: The Lamb on the throne guides to the springs of life

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-04-05.question: In Psalm 23:6, what follows David along with goodness?
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-04-05.learningObjective: Remember the term that shows the Lord's faithful love.
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-04-05.feedbackCorrect: Mercy is God's faithful love: it does not stay behind, it follows David every day.

feedbackWrong.a: Peace fits the psalm, but it is not the word in the verse.
feedbackWrong.c: Righteousness appears in Psalm 23:3, in the paths; here goodness has another partner.

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-04-05.hint: It is the faithful love that goes with David his whole life.

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-04-06.question: What links Psalm 23:1 to John 10:11?
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-04-06.learningObjective: Connect the shepherd of Psalm 23 to Jesus, as Jesus himself does.
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-04-06.feedbackCorrect: Jesus takes up the image of Psalm 23: he is the shepherd, and he gives his life for the sheep.

feedbackWrong.a: David places himself as a sheep; in John, the one who says "I am the good shepherd" is Jesus.
feedbackWrong.c: John 10 does not speak of church leaders; it speaks of Jesus and his sheep.

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-04-06.hint: See who speaks in the first person in John 10:11.

options.a: David is the good shepherd
options.b: Jesus is the good Shepherd
options.c: Pastors lead the churches

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-05-01.question: In John 1:8, John the Baptist is presented as the light that came into the world.
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-05-01.learningObjective: Observe that John the Baptist points to the light but is not the light.
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-05-01.feedbackCorrect: The text says the opposite: "Não era ele a luz". John came to bear witness to the light.

feedbackWrong.true: Reread John 1:8: John was not the light; he came to bear witness to the light.

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-05-01.hint: Look at the beginning of the verse.

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-05-02.question: In John 1:1, tap who was with God in the beginning.
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-05-02.learningObjective: Identify the Word as the one who was with God in the beginning.
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-05-02.feedbackCorrect: The Word was already with God in the beginning; John uses this name for Jesus.

feedbackWrong.b: "Era" is the verb of the sentence; tap who was with God.
feedbackWrong.c: "Princípio" tells when, not who.

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-05-02.hint: Look for the name that repeats three times in the verse.

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-05-03.question: According to John 1:12, what do those who welcome the Word receive?
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-05-03.learningObjective: Observe what John promises to those who receive the Word.
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-05-03.feedbackCorrect: Whoever receives the Word and believes in his name gains the right to become a child of God.

feedbackWrong.a: Verse 13 says these children are not born of blood, but of God.
feedbackWrong.b: The light here is Jesus; what is received is becoming a child of God.
feedbackWrong.d: The text does not speak of becoming a prophet; it speaks of becoming a child of God.

options.a: A guaranteed place among the people of Israel
options.b: The ability to see the light with their eyes
options.c: The right to become children of God
options.d: The right to be prophets like John

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-05-04.question: Put John 1:14 together in the order of the text.
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-05-04.feedbackCorrect: That is the verse's order: the Word comes to live among us, full of grace, and his glory is seen.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the Word becoming flesh; the glory seen comes at the end.

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-05-04.hint: The verse begins with the Word.

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-05-05.question: In John 1:5, where does the light shine?
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-05-05.learningObjective: Remember the image of the light shining in the dark.
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-05-05.feedbackCorrect: The light shines right in the dark, and the darkness cannot put it out.

feedbackWrong.a: Waters recall Genesis 1, but here the light shines in the dark.
feedbackWrong.b: The light does not stay far off, up high; it shines where it is dark.

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-05-05.hint: Think of the opposite of light.

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-05-06.question: What does John 1:14 say that connects to this context?
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-05-06.learningObjective: Connect John 1:14 to the human life of Jesus.
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-05-06.feedbackCorrect: "Se fez carne": the Word, who was God, came to live as a human being among us.

feedbackWrong.a: The text says the opposite: he lived among us.
feedbackWrong.c: John says "se fez carne": not an appearance, but a truly human life.

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-05-06.hint: See what the Word became and where he lived.

options.a: The Word stayed far away, in heaven
options.b: The Word became a human being
options.c: The Word appeared only as a vision

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-05-01.question: In John 1:10, the world was made through the Word, and even so it did not know him.
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-05-01.learningObjective: Understand the contrast between the Creator and the world that did not know him.
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-05-01.feedbackCorrect: "No entanto" marks the contrast: the world came from him, yet did not recognize him.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread John 1:10: the world was made through him; yet the world did not know him.

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-05-01.hint: Notice the expression that links the two parts of the verse.

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-05-02.question: In John 1:12, tap the word that marks the turn after the rejection in the previous verse.
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-05-02.learningObjective: Recognize the marker of contrast between rejection and welcome.
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-05-02.feedbackCorrect: "Mas" turns the page: his own did not receive him, but whoever does becomes a child of God.

feedbackWrong.a: "Deu-lhes" shows the gift received, not the turn itself.
feedbackWrong.b: "Todos" tells the reach; the turn comes before, in the first word.

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-05-02.hint: Look for a short word at the start of the verse.

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-05-03.question: In John 1:7–8, how does John the Baptist relate to the light?
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-05-03.learningObjective: Relate John the Baptist's mission to the light.
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-05-03.feedbackCorrect: John is a witness: he points to the light so that everyone may come to believe.

feedbackWrong.b: There is no rivalry: he came to bear witness about the light.
feedbackWrong.c: John 1:8 says: "Não era ele a luz".
feedbackWrong.d: The purpose is wide: "a fim de que todos viessem a crer".

options.a: He points to the light, so that others may believe
options.b: He competes with the light for the people's faith
options.c: He is the light, sent before the Word
options.d: He keeps the light only for his own disciples

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-05-04.question: In what order does John present the Word in John 1:1–14?
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-05-04.learningObjective: Understand the movement of John's prologue.
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-05-04.feedbackCorrect: First who he is, then what he did in creation, and then his coming to live among us.

feedbackWrong.default: John starts in the beginning, moves through creation, and arrives at the Word made flesh.

options.a: The eternal Word, with God and God
options.b: All things were made through him
options.c: The Word comes to live among us

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-05-05.question: In John 1:11, what did his own fail to do with the Word?
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-05-05.learningObjective: Remember the action that separates rejection from welcome.
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-05-05.feedbackCorrect: He came to his own, and they did not receive him: the rejection sets up the turn in verse 12.

feedbackWrong.a: "Conheceu" appears in John 1:10, about the world; here the verb is different.
feedbackWrong.c: The text does not speak of following; it speaks of welcoming the one who came.

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-05-05.hint: Verse 12 repeats the same verb, now in the positive.

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-05-06.question: What links John 1:1 to Genesis 1:1?
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-05-06.learningObjective: Relate the beginning of John to the beginning of Genesis.
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-05-06.feedbackCorrect: John begins like Genesis to show that the Word was already there when everything began.

feedbackWrong.a: In the beginning, the Word already was; he was not created.
feedbackWrong.c: John speaks of the same creation; all things were made through the Word.

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-05-06.hint: Compare the first words of the two verses.

options.a: The Word created in the beginning
options.b: The same opening: "No princípio"
options.c: Two different creations of the world

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-05-01.question: John 1:1–2 shows the Word already with God in the beginning, not as something God created later.
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-05-01.learningObjective: Distinguish the eternal Word from a creature.
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-05-01.feedbackCorrect: The Word already was in the beginning, was with God and was God; all things were made through him.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread: "No princípio, era o Verbo". He does not appear later; he was already beside God.

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-05-01.hint: See where the Word was in the beginning.

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-05-02.question: In John 1:5, tap the phrase that shows the light still stands in the face of evil.
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-05-02.learningObjective: Support from the text that the light is not overcome.
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-05-02.feedbackCorrect: Darkness is real, but it has not overcome the light: the last word belongs to the light.

feedbackWrong.a: "Nas trevas" shows where it shines, not how the clash ends.
feedbackWrong.b: "A luz" tells who shines; what shows it holds firm comes at the end.

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-05-02.hint: Look at what the darkness could not do.

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-05-03.question: What reading does John 1:14 support about how God makes himself known?
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-05-03.learningObjective: Choose the reading the text supports about God revealing himself in Jesus.
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-05-03.feedbackCorrect: The Word lived among us, and his glory was seen: in Jesus, God lets himself be known.

feedbackWrong.b: John says "vimos a sua glória": God let himself be seen up close.
feedbackWrong.c: "Se fez carne" affirms real humanity, not an appearance.
feedbackWrong.d: In the beginning, the Word already was, and was God (John 1:1).

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-05-03.hint: Compare each option with "habitou entre nós" and "vimos".

options.a: God shows himself in Jesus, who lived among us
options.b: God remains distant, and no one sees his glory
options.c: Jesus only seemed human, like an apparition
options.d: The Word was the first thing God created

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-05-04.question: Which sequence shows the thread of God living with his people that runs through John 1:14?
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-05-04.learningObjective: See John 1:14 within the thread of God coming to live with his people.
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-05-04.feedbackCorrect: From the tent in the desert to Jesus among us, and at last God living with his people.

feedbackWrong.default: Follow the story: the desert (Ex 40:34), Jesus (John 1:14), and the end (Rev 21:3).

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-05-04.hint: Follow the order of the Bible: Exodus, the Gospels, Revelation.

options.a: The glory of the Lord fills the tent in the desert
options.b: The Word dwells among us and we see his glory
options.c: God comes to live with his people forever

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-05-05.question: In John 1:14, what did the Word do among us after becoming flesh?
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-05-05.learningObjective: Remember the term that shows God coming to live close by.
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-05-05.feedbackCorrect: To dwell is to live alongside, like pitching a tent among the people: God truly near.

feedbackWrong.a: It was not a quick visit; the text speaks of living among the people.
feedbackWrong.c: He also spoke, but the verse says more: he lived among us.

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-05-05.hint: The verb is about living somewhere, not visiting.

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-05-06.question: What links John 1:3 to Hebrews 1:1–2?
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-05-06.learningObjective: Connect the creating Word in John to the Son in Hebrews.
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-05-06.feedbackCorrect: Both texts say the same thing: it was through the Son that God made all things.

feedbackWrong.a: The texts do not place the Son among the things made; all things were made through him.
feedbackWrong.c: The Son was already at work in creation: "through whom he also made the universe".

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-05-06.hint: See through whom things were made in both texts.

options.a: The Son was made first
options.b: All things were made by the Son
options.c: The Son came after creation
